s1.syndrome_frame: Malignant pleural disease with distant metastasis
salient_findings: Multiple pleural thickenings and marked effusion on the left side
Nodular growth on the mid third of the tongue
Epithelioid solid formations with pseudopapillary structures
key_facts: 62-year-old nonsmoking man
Multiple pleural thickenings and marked effusion on the left side
Underwent first-line chemotherapy followed by left pleurectomy
Postsurgical assessment revealed residual microscopic disease
External beam radiotherapy was administered
Disease remained stable until July 2023
Nodular growth appeared on the mid third of the tongue
Immunoreactive for calretinin, AE1/AE3, D2-40, Wilms tumor protein 1
Absence of nuclear staining for BRCA1-associated protein 1
Negative for methylthioadenosine phosphorylase
Homozygous deletion of CDKN2A gene by fluorescent in-situ hybridization

shortlist.label: Malignant pleural mesothelioma
shortlist.why_kept: Immunoreactive for calretinin, AE1/AE3, D2-40, Wilms tumor protein 1, and presence of pleural thickenings and effusion

shortlist.label: Desmoplastic malignant mesothelioma
shortlist.why_kept: Pleural involvement and epithelioid cell morphology

shortlist.label: Sarcomatoid malignant mesothelioma
shortlist.why_kept: Pleural involvement and presence of epithelioid cells

shortlist.label: Biphasic malignant mesothelioma
shortlist.why_kept: Pleural involvement and mixture of epithelioid and sarcomatoid components

shortlist.label: Epithelioid hemangioendothelioma
shortlist.why_kept: Epithelioid cell morphology and pleural involvement

raw.rationale: The patient's presentation with multiple pleural thickenings and marked effusion, along with immunoreactivity for calretinin, AE1/AE3, D2-40, and Wilms tumor protein 1, is consistent with malignant pleural mesothelioma. The disease's stability after treatment and subsequent development of a nodular growth on the tongue, which was found to be a metastasis with similar immunoreactive properties, further supports this diagnosis.

rejected.label: Desmoplastic malignant mesothelioma
rejected.why: The presence of epithelioid solid formations and pseudopapillary structures, rather than a predominantly desmoplastic pattern, makes this less likely.

rejected.label: Sarcomatoid malignant mesothelioma
rejected.why: The lack of spindle cell morphology and the presence of epithelioid cells in both the pleural and tongue lesions argue against this subtype.

rejected.label: Biphasic malignant mesothelioma
rejected.why: While biphasic mesothelioma contains both epithelioid and sarcomatoid components, the described pathology primarily highlights epithelioid features without clear evidence of a significant sarcomatoid component.

rejected.label: Epithelioid hemangioendothelioma
rejected.why: The immunoreactivity profile, particularly the positivity for calretinin and Wilms tumor protein 1, and the clinical presentation are more consistent with malignant mesothelioma than epithelioid hemangioendothelioma.
